PEMBROKE, Bermuda--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Gold Reserve Ltd. (TSX.V: GRZ) (BSX: GRZ.BH) (OTCQX: GDRZF) (“Gold Reserve” or the “Company”) announced today that it intends to make final offers to holders of its outstanding contingent value rights (“CVRs”) and to participants in its 2012 bonus plan (“Bonus Plan”) to settle all or a portion of their respective entitlements in exchange for a cash payment. The Company previously reported its intention to make such offers in August 2026.

The proposed settlement offers are expected to be made on substantially the same terms as the settlement offers previously made by the Company to CVR holders and Bonus Plan participants earlier in 2026. The proposed settlement offers are expected to remain open for a limited period and to expire in early December 2026, on a specific date to be determined by the Company and communicated to the applicable CVR holders and Bonus Plan participants.

Further details regarding the proposed settlement offers, including the applicable terms and expiry date, will be communicated directly to CVR holders and Bonus Plan participants in due course.

The Company also provided an update in respect to its previously announced intention to offer holders of options expiring in February 2027 the opportunity to surrender their options in exchange for a cash payment at a discount to the market price. Following further consideration, management has determined not to proceed with the proposed offer at this time; however, management may consider offers at a later date. Holders of outstanding options retain the ability to exercise their options, including through cashless and net exercise, in accordance with the terms of the Company’s amended equity incentive plan.

About Gold Reserve

Gold Reserve is a primarily US-owned mineral exploration and development company, domiciled in Bermuda, focused on advancing high-quality mineral assets with the objective of creating sustainable long-term value for shareholders. The Company is listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (TSX-V: GRZ), the Bermuda Stock Exchange (BSX: GRZ.BH), and trades in the United States on the OTCQX (OTCQX: GDRZF).

Improvements to security, cost, and team experience advance the governed software factory for every enterprise 

  • Agentic remediation helps security teams shrink vulnerability backlogs and prioritize exploitable flaws by real risk.
  • Scheduled automations, now in beta, let GitLab Duo Agent Platform flows handle routine tasks in the background, on a cadence each organization chooses and within the controls it sets.
  • GitLab for Slack, now generally available on GitLab.com, lets teams mention @GitLab in a thread to turn decisions into issues, merge requests, and agent flows.
  • GitLab has made agentic usage on GitLab Duo Agent Platform more efficient, so most customers will see their GitLab Credits go up to twice as far.

SAN FRANCISCO--(BUSINESS WIRE)--All Remote - GitLab Inc., the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps, today announced GitLab 19.6, with new capabilities that help security teams work down vulnerability backlogs, make GitLab Credits go further, automate recurring tasks, and bring agents into Slack conversations where teams make decisions. These capabilities help organizations put agents to work across more of the software lifecycle while keeping visibility and control over agent activity and spending.

Engineering, security, and product teams now use agents for a wider range of tasks. As that use grows, organizations need the cost of agent work to stay manageable. They also need automation that lets agents move work forward without someone starting each task. GitLab 19.6 delivers both, with controls that show which agent acted, what it could access, and what it did.

Reducing Vulnerability Backlogs With Agentic Remediation

Every team is adding security findings faster than they can clear them. GitLab 19.6 extends agentic remediation so GitLab Duo security agents can work through more of that backlog. Security managers can turn on agent flows across many projects at once, and teams can run those flows on branches other than the default to fix findings before code merges.

A new vulnerability context flow, in beta for SAST findings, shows whether a flaw is exploitable in practice, so teams can prioritize by exploitability as well as severity. A new mean time to remediation chart shows whether remediation keeps pace with discovery, and group-level policies hold changes with critical or known-exploited vulnerabilities until a designated approver signs off.

When secret detection finds an active GitLab personal access token, teams can now rotate it and fix the code in one step. Rotate and fix, now in beta on GitLab.com, revokes the leaked token, creates a replacement with the same permissions, and stores it in GitLab Secrets Manager. GitLab Duo then opens a merge request that removes the hardcoded token from the code.

Scheduling Recurring Agent Tasks

Recurring tasks such as issue triage wait on a person or an event to start them, so teams complete them late or not at all. Scheduled automations, now in beta, run GitLab Duo Agent Platform flows in the background on a set cadence, from every 15 minutes to every three months. A team can triage new issues daily, or check CI health every hour and post the likely root cause before anyone starts investigating.

Each automation runs as a dedicated service account with scoped permissions, so audit events separate agent activity from human activity and record every change. A redesigned Automations page shows what ran, how often it succeeded, and why a run failed. These controls make scheduled automations a building block of the governed software factory.

Bringing Agents Into Slack Conversations

Software decisions often start in Slack, and someone then retypes them into GitLab. GitLab for Slack lets teams mention @GitLab in a thread or direct message to turn those decisions into issues, merge requests, and agent flows. The agent posts results back to the thread.

Each request runs with the requester's own GitLab permissions, creates an agent session in GitLab, and draws from GitLab Credits. Merge requests follow the same reviews, approvals, and audit trail as any other change.

GitLab for Slack is now generally available on GitLab.com for Premium and Ultimate customers, and GitLab plans to add support for GitLab Self-Managed next month.

Each GitLab Credit Now Does Up to Twice the Work

GitLab has made agentic usage on GitLab Duo Agent Platform more efficient and is passing those savings on to customers. Each task given to Duo Agent Platform now results in fewer model requests, such that most customers will see their GitLab Credits go up to twice as far.

Organizations can use the freed-up credits for the new agentic remediation and scheduled automations, and to extend agentic work to Slack. Customers who have Flex contracts can also use available credits for recently introduced innovations such as GitLab Secrets Manager, Dedicated Hosted Runners, and coming soon, GitLab Orbit. This builds on recent tools for managing credit spend, including impact and cost analytics to track usage and manage credit caps.

The change takes effect on November 19, 2026, for new customers. Existing customers move to it on December 18 or can opt in earlier.

GitLab 19.6 also includes the following updates:

  • MCP governance. With new controls now in beta, group owners can set each GitLab MCP server tool to Always Allow, Always Ask, or Always Deny, and every tool call through the MCP server now creates an audit event. Security teams control what agents can do in GitLab and keep a record of everything they did.
  • GitLab Duo flows from the tools developers already use. When Claude Code, Cursor, or another MCP client connects, the GitLab MCP server suggests a matching GitLab Duo flow and confirms before starting it. Developers hand work to GitLab agents without switching tools.
  • Rapid Diffs. A rebuilt merge request view, now generally available, loads the first file about three times faster. Reviews start in seconds, even on large merge requests.
  • Resumable jobs and auto-merge time windows. Agent sessions can pause and resume where they left off, and teams can set a time window for auto-merge. Long-running agent work doesn't have to start over, and changes merge only when the team is ready.

To learn more about the 19.6 release, please read the what's new page. Teams can also find guidance on building and scaling with agents in the AI-Native Engineering Playbook and GitLab Well Architected guide.

Supporting Quotes

  • “Teams make decisions in Slack every day, and the best agents are the ones that can act on that context,” said Katie Steigman, vice president product management, Slack. “GitLab for Slack lets agents read the conversation, take action across the software lifecycle in GitLab, and bring the results back to the thread. Teams can go from a quick discussion to planned, reviewed, and shipped work without switching tools.”
  • “Every organization is racing to keep up with the security challenges that have become the new norm,” said Manav Khurana, chief product and marketing officer, GitLab. “GitLab 19.6 helps security teams clear vulnerability backlogs faster, and provides new automations. Both of which are easier to afford now that each GitLab Credit can be used for more agentic work.”

About GitLab

GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 70 million registered users and approximately 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster. *Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Key Terms

personal access tokentechnical
A personal access token is a string of characters issued by a software service to authenticate a specific user or automated process when accessing that service (for example APIs, repositories, or developer tools). It functions like a password but is typically created for a particular account and purpose, can be limited to specific permissions or scopes, may have an expiration time, and can be revoked independently of the user’s main password. Because the token carries the access rights granted when it was created, anyone holding it can perform actions allowed by its scopes until it is revoked or expires.

Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Emerita Resources Corp. (TSXV: EMO) (OTCQX: EMOTF) (FSE: LLJA) (the "Company" or "Emerita") presents Executive Chairman letter

Dear Fellow Shareholders,

Following my November 16th letter to Emerita shareholders, Mr. Peters issued an immediate rebuttal. He raises numerous accusations and demands yet offers few practical solutions to delivering tangible value for Emerita shareholders. His response also contains statements that misrepresent the Company's position, omit important facts, and oversimplify decisions that require careful judgment.

This type of impulsive response from Mr. Peters is becoming a pattern. His approach to consequential strategic decisions raises concerns about the judgment required to lead a public mining company. Shareholders deserve directors who examine facts, process and consequences before acting.

I will address the points in Mr. Peters' latest response methodically, with facts, and ask the questions his statements leave unanswered.

Emerita's need for capital
Mr. Peters states, "The Company can raise equity capital but we have asked that any shares issued before the meeting do not vote at the meeting" and that "Any strategic investor should have no issue with that".

This statement is not grounded in reality. What investor, especially a sophisticated strategic investor, would invest equity in a company where the outcome and direction of the company is unknown due to a potential fundamental change in the board and significant shift in strategy?

Mr. Peters is free to exercise his rights as a shareholder of the Company, however, the uncertainty created by his requisition and premature attempts to frustrate Emerita's ability to raise capital is one of the reasons for the Board's decision to undertake the strategic review process announced on November 16th.

In addition, we should not speculate what our lender may or may not approve in respect of the Company's credit facility. Mr. Peters' oversimplification of our credit facility should not be interpreted by shareholders as committed immediately available liquidity.

A Strategic Review is an opportunity for shareholders
Mr. Peters has questioned why the strategic review will proceed independently of the requisitioned meeting. The reason is straightforward: protecting shareholder value.

I would ask shareholders to consider another question: What would be gained by preventing the Board from exploring an opportunity that might preserve the option value of their investment?

Emerita's financial and operational obligations continue regardless of the potential proxy contest. The Board cannot suspend its responsibilities because a shareholder wants to hold another vote.

The Board will evaluate potential alternatives. Where a proposed transaction requires shareholder approval, shareholders will decide through the applicable approval process. Mr. Peters should understand that conducting a strategic review for a public company neither deprives shareholders of their rights nor removes the Board's duty to consider opportunities.

Mr. Peters should also understand that a public company conducting a strategic review must respect confidentiality obligations to potential counterparties and applicable disclosure rules. Emerita will update shareholders when legally and commercially appropriate.

Commitment to our Core Business: IBW
Mr. Peters claims to support Emerita's mining business in Spain, yet he offers no concrete plan to advance IBW. He has not identified relevant mining experience of his own. Emerita's current Board includes directors with substantial mining and project experience and fluency in Spanish, including Joseph Belan and Oscar Cabrera and Peter McRae. Mr. Peters should explain what superior capabilities his proposed Board would bring to developing a mining project in Spain.

Mr. Peters says he wants Agne Ahlenius and Joaquin Merino to remain. Mr. Merino is Emerita's Chief Executive Officer and already has the Board's support. Messrs. Merino and Ahlenius have already reiterated their support for your Board.

What the August Meeting was really about
Mr. Peters has mistaken support for change in August as a mandate for his current proposals. He is wrong.

Mr. Peters now describes the August withhold campaign as a vote about who should oversee Falcon. As you know, the campaign centered on whether three longstanding directors should continue to serve on the Board. Your Board respects shareholders' decisions.

The current requisition presents a different question: whether Mr. Peters and his nominees should be given effective control of the Board while the Company faces financing, development and litigation decisions.

Shareholders have told me that the continuing disruption and expense of Mr. Peters' campaign risks making Emerita's already difficult position worse. That concern belongs in the assessment of whether another fight over the Board creates any shareholder value.

Falcon: Where is the Evidence of an alleged Improper Settlement?
Mr. Peters continues to suggest that the Board may rush into an improper settlement of Emerita's Falcon claims. What evidence supports that serious allegation? His suggestion is another example of raising fears about a complex matter without identifying any concrete proposed settlement or an improper Board decision.

The Company has received information from concerned shareholders that Mr. Peters has had at least one discussion with representatives of Lithium Ionic concerning Falcon. Shareholders deserve to know whether anything regarding a potential settlement was discussed by Mr. Peters.

Serious Omissions Raise Questions About Mr. Peter's Agenda — Is There Full Transparency?
As part of our ongoing review of matters related to Mr. Peters and parties close to him, one of the most troubling discrepancies we have identified concerns Mr. Peters' intentions regarding his Board composition.

In the November 3 announcement of his requisition, and as stated on their website, the Concerned Shareholders identified three proposed directors: Andrew Elinesky, Norman Findlay, and Wayne Peters. Yet letters dated November 3 from Mr. Peters' legal counsel to the Ontario Securities Commission and the TSX Venture Exchange describe clear intentions to appoint a fourth individual to the Board: Robin Bienenstock. In other words, shareholders were publicly told about three nominees, while regulators received correspondence confirming Mr. Peters' intention to name four — Ms. Bienenstock is his undisclosed candidate to fill the current vacancy on your Board.

Why did Mr. Peters disclose four directors to regulators while telling shareholders about only three?

Mr. Peters has repeatedly demanded transparency and accountability from Emerita's Board ("Operation Transparency" as he calls it). Shareholders are entitled to expect the same from someone seeking substantial influence over their Company. His public statements and regulatory correspondence should tell the same story. Until he explains the discrepancy, shareholders have reason to question whether they have been given a complete account of his intentions.

Mr. Peters says his group holds only about 5% of the outstanding shares and is therefore a long way from controlling Emerita. His campaign seeks to replace a majority of the Board, and he has included himself as a nominee. If successful, he and his disclosed (and undisclosed) members would collectively exercise effective influence over the Board.

Mr. Peters Has Misrepresented Emerita's Board Appointments Press Release
Mr. Peters cites the September 16 announcement as if it proves departing directors chose their replacements. It does not.

The release thanked Catherine Stretch and Marilia Bento for assisting during the transition. It did not say they voted on their successors. As I confirmed on November 16, the directors who received majority-withhold votes did not participate in the appointment decision.

A statement of thanks is exactly that, and nothing more.

Read the Room
Shareholders are asking why Emerita should endure another disruptive Board contest when qualified directors are already in place, and the Company faces substantial financial, legal and operating challenges. They have told me that they want the Board focused on stabilizing the Company and advancing its assets.

Mr. Peters continues to present himself as the "Voice of Emerita". He is just one (loud) voice, but he does not speak for all Shareholders.

Shareholders I have spoken with tell me his current demands are increasingly out of step with what they want. They supported specific changes in August and recognize that those changes occurred. They now want the Company stabilized and focused on creating value. They are concerned about the consequences of another prolonged fight over the Board.

The Value Equation
Proxy contests ultimately centre on who has a credible strategy to create and realize shareholder value. A list of criticisms and individual proposals is not a strategy. Proposals must fit together and be capable of successful execution.

Mr. Peters has no shortage of lawyers, press releases and online commentators advancing his arguments. Shareholders have heard far less from him about how he would advance IBW and realize value from Falcon. Those are the strategic questions that matter.

The IBW PFS: We Are Providing More Information
Mr. Peters suggests that the Company failed to explain the economics of the IBW Pre-Feasibility Study.

As I acknowledged in my November 16 letter, questions about the PFS and its assumptions are expected in the normal course. Emerita has posted an updated company presentation on its website to address certain questions and explain the development path for IBW. We will provide further clarification where necessary.

An Honest Dialogue with Shareholders
I will continue engaging with shareholders and listening to their concerns. I welcome scrutiny of your Board. I expect shareholders to challenge us, question our decisions and hold us accountable.

I am confident that your Board has the right experience to navigate Emerita's present challenges. We will pursue the strategic review and other credible alternatives for protecting and realizing value for Emerita, its shareholders and stakeholders.

Sincerely,

Joseph Belan
Executive Chairman
Emerita Resources Corp.

PALO ALTO, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Guardant Health, Inc. (Nasdaq: GH), a leading precision oncology company, today announced the U.S. clinical launch of Guardant Reveal® Ultra, a new molecular residual disease (MRD) platform for solid tumors offering personalized, ultra-sensitive detection of residual cancer. Built on Guardant’s Smart Platform, Reveal Ultra incorporates tumor-informed, patient-specific genomic alterations to provide one of the most advanced and actionable views of MRD.

Validated on thousands of clinical samples, Guardant Reveal Ultra has demonstrated detection sensitivity of 1 part per million (ppm) or below across major tumor types. The test incorporates patient-specific alterations from thousands of genomic targets spanning all major variant classes, including structural variants. Guardant Reveal Ultra has also been validated with tissue samples containing as little as 5% tumor cellularity, significantly below the typical industry requirement of 20%, enabling testing across a broader range of clinical specimens.

“Reveal Ultra opens a new frontier in MRD detection,” said Helmy Eltoukhy, Guardant Health chairman and co-CEO. “While detecting cancer at one part per million has become an important benchmark, what truly matters is delivering that level of sensitivity reliably across real clinical samples and a broad range of tumor types. Reveal Ultra was built to meet that challenge, bringing extraordinary precision to everyday clinical practice and advancing our ability to track and manage each patient’s cancer throughout their journey.”

Guardant Reveal Ultra is designed as a connected experience, enabling physicians the option of a direct path from MRD detection to clinical action through Guardant360® Liquid. Together with Guardant Reveal®’s best-in-class tissue-free MRD detection and therapy monitoring capabilities, and Guardant360 Liquid and Guardant360® Tissue for comprehensive genomic profiling, Guardant Reveal Ultra completes Guardant’s precision oncology portfolio. These solutions work hand-in-hand to support physicians in selecting therapies, monitoring treatment response, detecting residual disease, and managing cancer throughout the patient journey.

Guardant Health is a leading precision oncology company focused on guarding wellness and giving every person more time free from cancer. Key Terms

molecular residual diseasemedical
Molecular residual disease is the tiny amount of cancer that can remain in the body after treatment and is detectable only by sensitive tests that find cancer DNA or other molecular traces. It matters to investors because these measurements can predict relapse, guide whether additional therapy is needed, and shape the market for diagnostics and drugs—much like finding embers after a fire helps decide if more firefighting is required.
structural variantstechnical
Structural variants are large-scale changes in an organism’s DNA—such as missing, extra, flipped, or rearranged chunks of genetic material—that are like tearing out, duplicating, or reshuffling chapters in a book. Investors should care because these changes can drive or explain diseases, alter how well diagnostics and therapies work, and shift the commercial and regulatory outlook for drugs, tests, and gene-based treatments.
tumor cellularitymedical
The proportion of a tissue sample that is made up of actual tumor (malignant) cells rather than non-malignant components such as stroma, inflammatory cells, blood, or necrotic debris; expressed as a percentage of tumor cells among the nucleated cells in the specimen. Tumor cellularity is assessed by a pathologist on the biopsy or surgical specimen and affects how reliable molecular tests (like DNA sequencing or biomarker assays) are because low cellularity can dilute tumor-derived signals; it can also vary within and between samples due to tumor heterogeneity and sampling or processing factors.

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - New Zealand Energy Corp. (TSXV: NZ) ("NZEC" or the "Company") is pleased to announce a non-brokered private placement (the "Offering") for gross proceeds of up to C$3,000,000, the commencement of its planned oil well workover campaign, and continued solid production from the Tariki 1A well.

Private Placement

The Company intends to complete the Offering of common shares of the Company (each, a "Common Share") at a price of C$0.35 per Common Share for aggregate gross proceeds of up to C$3,000,000.

The net proceeds of the Offering are expected to be used to ensure the Company has sufficient working capital to undertake operations on the Tariki Gas Storage Project, to fund the Company's share of active oil well interventions, to bring the Tariki 5A well onto long-term production, and for general working capital purposes.

The Company is also preparing to order long lead items related to the gas storage project and is working to secure a significant lending package to support the funding of the development costs. In connection with the anticipated capital facility, the Company intends to ensure it has sufficient working capital to carry the Tariki Gas Storage Project through to a final investment decision.

The Offering is expected to close on or about November 30, 2026. Closing of the Offering is subject to the receipt of all necessary regulatory approvals, including the approval of the TSX Venture Exchange (the "TSXV"). All Common Shares issued pursuant to the Offering will be subject to a hold period of four months and one day from the date of issuance in accordance with applicable Canadian securities laws and the policies of the TSXV. The Company may pay finders' fees in connection with the Offering.

Oil Operations

NZEC expects to commence its planned oil well workover campaign shortly. Over the next few months, the Company expects to add over 800 barrels of oil per day (gross) of production through well clean-outs, additional perforations, and pump additions on its Ngaere and Waihapa wells.

In addition, working with the Company's joint venture partner, Monumental Energy Corp. (TSXV: MNRG), the Company has received promising initial laboratory results using flow assurance chemicals, and a pilot trial will be undertaken at Copper Moki to test the potential uplift in production.

Tariki Production

The Tariki 1A well continues to deliver consistent stabilized flow rates of approximately 2.5 MMcf/d (gross) and has been dewatering the Tariki reservoir at approximately 1,600 barrels of water per day. The well forms part of Petroleum Mining Licence PML 38138, in which NZEC holds a 50% interest. The Company's activities at Tariki are conducted together with its co-venturer, L&M Energy Limited.

NZEC continues to focus on optimizing production through debottlenecking work at its Waihapa production station and is evaluating providing third-party access to several groups, subject to the success of their exploration activities.

Toby Pierce, Chief Executive Officer of NZEC, commented: "We continue to methodically advance the gas storage project and remain in active commercial discussions to both fund and build the project in due course. Further, given the elevated Brent oil prices at the moment, advancing our oil production is a key growth driver for the Company."

CHARLOTTE, N.C., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- First Horizon Bank (NYSE: FHN) (or "First Horizon") is proud to announce the official grand opening of its Charlotte corporate office at 110 East Boulevard. Centrally located in the Queen City's popular South End neighborhood, the office is positioned for the team to build and strengthen relationships with clients across the Charlotte area, and it enables First Horizon to serve the community as the company continues to expand its footprint across the region.

First Horizon is the anchor tenant at 110 East, a 24-story tower located in the city's East Boulevard corridor. Prominent First Horizon signage placement on the north and south sides of the building not only enhance the city's skyline, they signal the bank's commitment to the Charlotte community.

"We plan to be in Charlotte for the long term, and this office is a visible sign of that. Our name on the Charlotte skyline says we intend to keep earning the trust of the people and businesses we serve here," said Bryan Jordan, Chairman of the Board, President and Chief Executive Officer of First Horizon.

"Charlotte is the epicenter of our Mid-Atlantic region, and our clients expect us to show up with the same energy and ambition they bring to their own work," said Laura Bunn, Executive Vice President and Mid-Atlantic Regional President for First Horizon Bank. "110 East provides an ideal location to meet people and businesses where they are, from Uptown to the city's surrounding communities."

First Horizon will host various events throughout the year and support community involvement efforts that enhance the places where clients and associates work, live and serve.

For more information on First Horizon Bank and the Charlotte team, visit www.firsthorizon.com.
